summary: We developed an interactive digital museum that explores the history of abandoned artifacts specifically focusing on the Moon and Mars. It addresses the challenge by helping visitors discover their historical and scientific importance. Using interactive planet surfaces, numbered artifacts, images and spoken audio, users can explore and expand their knowledge of space exploration, instead of presenting information through ordinary text. Our project aims to make space history more engaging and accessible by presenting important exploration equipment in a creative manner.
details:
Space Graveyard is an interactive digital museum that takes visitors on a journey through the Moon and Mars to discover the objects humans have left behind during space exploration. Visitors can choose either planet, explore its surface, and click on numbered markers to learn about different artifacts through pictures and spoken explanations.

The main idea behind this project is to show that even objects left behind in space have stories worth telling. It helps people learn about space exploration in a more interesting and interactive way, rather than simply reading information from a textbook. We hope it encourages curiosity about space, makes scientific knowledge easier to understand, and reminds people of the achievements behind every mission.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend, Vite as our development and build tool, and Python with Flask for the backend. We also used GSAP for animations, Blender for creating 3D assets, and audio features to make the experience more engaging.

What makes our project creative is its museum concept. Instead of presenting abandoned space objects as ordinary historical information, we give them a place where visitors can explore and discover their stories. While developing it, we considered ease of use, visual design, accessibility of information, and how to make the experience engaging for visitors.
